title: AdPulse — Ad Event Streaming Pipeline and ClickHouse Query API

workstreams.title: Kafka/Flink ingestion, reconciliation and collector reliability
workstreams.summary: Kafka-to-Flink measurement pipeline for advertising events - validation, deduplication, normalization, impression/click/conversion joins, CDC historical dimensions and metric aggregation into Kafka result topics - with reconciliation and collector-reliability checks on synthetic data. The Flink stage uses the SQL and DataStream APIs with embedded RocksDB state.
bullets: Completed a simulated full data reconciliation over 3,949,000 synthetic advertising records with 0 unmatched rows and 0 duplicate business effects, comparing receipt, disk-reference and database business results by business key and value.

Built the Flink stage of the streaming pipeline: it consumes synthetic advertising events from Kafka, validates, deduplicates and normalizes them, joins impressions, clicks and conversions, enriches them with CDC-backed historical dimensions, and aggregates metrics into Kafka result topics.

Verified admission control on the collector's single Kafka transaction slot in a cloud stress test of 50 concurrent requests: 1 admitted and 49 rejected while 9/9 independent health probes passed; a fenced Kafka transactional producer stops admitting input until explicitly replaced, and a cancelled request keeps its slot until the native Kafka call returns.

Cut the reconciliation reference process's median peak RSS from 1,100,000 KiB to 139,700 KiB (87.3% lower) on 206,000 synthetic records in a fixed 2 CPU / 4 GiB environment by moving joins and sorting onto disk with SQLite, trading 2.29x elapsed time (32.0 s to 73.28 s, cold index build included) and 605 MiB temporary disk, with identical output hashes in 3/3 paired runs.

workstreams.title: Release-pinned bounded ClickHouse query API
workstreams.summary: Release-pinned query API over ClickHouse: the historical query benchmark ran on ClickHouse 24.8, and the later migration and the current deployment configuration use ClickHouse 26.3.32.14.
bullets: Cut median first-page query time from 622 ms to 32.9 ms (94.71% lower), timed from query-function entry to result-object return, by pushing filtering and keyset pagination into SQL instead of loading the whole release into Python, in an independent cloud 21,667-row, limit-100 experiment on synthetic data pinned to ClickHouse 24.8 (the historical benchmark version, later migrated to 26.3.32.14) and Python 3.12.
Lowered the first page's traced Python peak allocation from 71,300,000 B to 399,000 B (99.44%, decimal MB, not RSS) over five alternating paired runs after warmup.

Traversed 44 pages (43×500 + 167 = 21,667 rows) across 21 PostgreSQL active-release switches with no missing or duplicate rows in a cloud synthetic run, by pinning pagination to immutable releases with HMAC-signed cursors that bind release ID, filters, sort keys and original expiry; an expired cursor gets 503 with no renewal.
